\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Padding after the last true bit]
\lean{Complexity.splitAtLastTrue_pad}
\label{Complexity.splitAtLastTrue_pad}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.splitAtLastTrue}
\difficulty{4}
For every Boolean word $u$ and natural number $m$, cutting the word $u$ followed by a
true bit and then $m$ false bits at its last true bit returns $u$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Padded circuit encoding]
\lean{Complexity.padAdvice}
\label{Complexity.padAdvice}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.encode, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily}
Let $C=(C_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a family of Boolean circuits, let
$A:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and write $e_n$ for the Boolean-string encoding of $C_n$.
The padded string at length $n$ is $e_n$ followed by a true bit and then by
$\max(A(n)-|e_n|-1,0)$ false bits, where the subtraction is truncated at zero.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Length of padded circuit advice]
\lean{Complexity.length_padAdvice}
\label{Complexity.length_padAdvice}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.encode, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily, Complexity.padAdvice}
\difficulty{3}
Let $C$ be a family of directed acyclic circuits, let $A:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be a
length bound, and let $n\in\mathbb{N}$. If the encoding of the circuit $C(n)$ has length
at least one less than $A(n)$, then the padded advice string for $C$, $A$, and $n$ has
length exactly $A(n)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Circuit evaluation from its encoding]
\lean{Complexity.verdict_encode}
\label{Complexity.verdict_encode}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.verdict, BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.verdict_pairEncode, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.IsFaninTwo, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.encode, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.encode_injective, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.eq_of_encode_eq, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.eval, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $C$ be a Boolean directed acyclic circuit with $m$ input vertices, with distinct
arguments at each gate, exactly one argument at every NOT gate, and at most two
arguments at every gate. For every bit string $x$ of length $m$, the circuit evaluator
applied to the encoding of $C$ paired with $x$ returns the same Boolean value as
evaluating $C$ on the input assignment that gives input $i$ the bit at position $i$ of
$x$ (using $0$ when that position is absent).
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of a power bound]
\lean{Complexity.mul_pow_le_mul_pow_succ}
\label{Complexity.mul_pow_le_mul_pow_succ}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $C$, $n$, and $d$, one has $C(n+1)^d \le C(n+1)^{d+1}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Encoded circuits compute their language]
\lean{Complexity.verdict_encode_family}
\label{Complexity.verdict_encode_family}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.verdict, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.encode, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.eval, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily.HasFaninTwo, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily.language, Complexity.verdict_encode, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $C$ be a family of Boolean directed acyclic circuits, one for each input length, and
suppose every circuit in the family is well formed and has at most two arguments at each
gate. For every bit string $x$, the evaluator on the encoding of the circuit for length
$|x|$ paired with $x$ gives the indicator of the language accepted by the family on $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial bound from an input length bound]
\lean{Complexity.time_le_of_length_le}
\label{Complexity.time_le_of_length_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.succ_pow_le}
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $K,e,B,D,n,m$, if $m+1\le B(n+1)^D$, then
\[
K(m+1)^e\le K B^e 2^{De}(n^{De}+1).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Circuit size yields polynomial-time advice]
\lean{Complexity.mem_DTIMEAdvice_of_inSIZE}
\label{Complexity.mem_DTIMEAdvice_of_inSIZE}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.evalTM, BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.evalTM_computes, BoolCircuit.CircuitEval.verdict, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.encode, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.length_encode_le_of_isFaninTwo, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.size, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuitFamily.language, Complexity.DTIMEAdvice, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode, Complexity.length_padAdvice, Complexity.mul_pow_le_mul_pow_succ, Complexity.padAdvice, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_of_linear, Complexity.splitAtLastTrue_pad, Complexity.time_le_of_length_le, Complexity.verdict_encode_family, Language.InSIZE, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairFst, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairSnd, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_stripLast, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator, Turing.pairDecode_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{6}
Let $L$ be a language of finite binary words, and let $a,k\in\mathbb N$. If $L$ has a
family of Boolean circuits with fan-in at most two whose circuit on inputs of length $n$
has size at most $a(n+1)^k$, then there is a natural number $c$ such that $L$ is
decidable by a finite Turing machine with advice of length $(12a^2+1)(n+1)^{2k}$ and
running time at most a constant multiple of $n^c+1$ on inputs of length $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Circuit languages have polynomial advice algorithms]
\lean{Complexity.PPoly_subset_PAdvicePoly}
\label{Complexity.PPoly_subset_PAdvicePoly}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.DTIMEAdvice_subset_PAdvicePoly, Complexity.PAdvicePoly, Complexity.mem_DTIMEAdvice_of_inSIZE, Language.InPPoly}
\difficulty{3}
Every language recognized by a family of Boolean circuits with fan-in at most two and
size at most $a(n+1)^k$ on inputs of length $n$, for some natural numbers $a,k$, is
decidable by a deterministic finite Turing machine given an advice string depending only
on the input length. For some natural numbers $c,C,d$, the advice string for length $n$
has exactly $C(n+1)^d$ bits, and the machine decides the language on every input of
length $n$ within $c(n^c+1)$ steps when given the input and advice in the stated pair
encoding.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Natural numbers bounded by powers]
\lean{Complexity.le_pow_self_of_two_le}
\label{Complexity.le_pow_self_of_two_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
For any natural numbers $m$ and $n$ with $2 \le n$, one has $m \le n^m$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[A polynomial factor bounded by a power]
\lean{Complexity.mul_succ_pow_le_pow}
\label{Complexity.mul_succ_pow_le_pow}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.le_pow_self_of_two_le}
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $m$, $k$, and $n$ with $2\le n$, one has $(m+1)(n+1)^{2k}\le
n^{m+1+4k}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial-time bounded-length test]
\lean{Complexity.polyTimeComputable_lenFstLe}
\label{Complexity.polyTimeComputable_lenFstLe}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_const, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_lenLe, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairFstD}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $m$, the function sending a bit string $z$ to the one-bit word
$1$ when $|\pi_1(z)|\le m$ and to $0$ otherwise is polynomial-time computable, where
$\pi_1$ is the total first projection that returns the empty word when decoding fails.
\end{lemma}
